subject: BridgePoint integration: inference + tool-calling architecture follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@bridgepoint.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + tech asks (tool calling + reranker)

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the call this morning — good to meet the team. Quick recap from BridgePoint's side and a handful of technical questions so we can scope a 2-week POC: 

1) Goals for the POC
- Replace current heuristics for invoice routing with an LLM-driven workflow + tools: (a) invoice_fetcher (internal API), (b) fraud_check (third-party), (c) payment_processor. We want the system to call tools when the model flags an invoicing action.
- Provide embeddings-based retrieval over our 12k invoice PDFs and an in-session reranker to surface the top 3 candidate matches for reconciliation.

2) Non-functional targets
- 95th pct latency for user-visible flows < 600ms (aim for < 300ms for auth+router hop).
- PII/PCI: payment_processor calls must run in a PCI-isolated environment.

3) Tech asks (we need this to scope integration effort)
- SDK: Can your SDK be used inside our node-based microservices? Any quickstart for function/tool definitions?
- Auth: Best practices for scoping API keys for tool calls (service-account per tool vs token scopes).
- Routing: Can we route certain tool calls to a private deployment (for PCI) while keeping general generation on hosted API?
- Tool calling: Interested in parallel invocation of invoice_fetcher + fraud_check and then merging/reranking results. Any recommended patterns?
- Structured output: We need strict contract enforcement from the model for tool invocation (tool name + JSON args), and graceful handling if the model returns an unknown tool or malformed JSON.

If you could send an integration sketch, sample tool-def contract, and the SDK quickstart + any caveats for parallel tool calls that would be great.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Integrations, BridgePoint

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@bridgepoint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jul 2028 11:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick recap + tech asks (tool calling + reranker)

Thanks Alex — great summary. Short answers first, then proposed next steps and a lightweight architecture sketch.

Short answers
- SDK: Yes — our Node SDK supports both browser and server runtimes; recommended pattern is the Redwood client + a small adapter for injecting per-request auth (examples attached in redwood-sdk-quickstart.md).
- Auth: We typically recommend short-lived service tokens scoped per-tool for cross-service calls (service-account per sensitive tool like payment_processor). This gives least privilege and easier rotation/audit.
- Routing: Supported. Policy can route by tool tag ("pci=true") to your private deployment or VPC-hosted endpoint; fallback to hosted variants if private pool is saturated.
- Tool calling pattern: Parallel invocation is supported — call invoice_fetcher and fraud_check concurrently, then assemble a combined result and run a reranker model (or use a rerank endpoint) to produce the final ordered set. See notes below on partial failures.
- Structured output: We recommend an enforced tool-def schema. Our runtime enforces tool names and field types before executing (and will surface a structured validation error back to the model).

Architecture sketch (high level)
1) Frontend -> Redwood hosted API (generation + safety hooks) for user prompt parsing and intent classification.
2) Redwood runtime emits tool call directives. A routing policy evaluates tool tags:
   - If tool.tag == "pci" -> route to Private deployment endpoint (VPC) with service-account token for payment_processor.
   - Else -> call internal microservice via Redwood-hosted connector or call directly from your service using short-lived scoped token.
3) Parallel tool execution pattern:
   - Invoke invoice_fetcher and fraud_check in parallel (async).
   - Use a small orchestration layer (we can provide an orchestration helper in SDK) to collect results with per-call timeouts (e.g., 250ms for fraud_check, 500ms for invoice_fetcher).
   - If one tool times out, mark partial result and proceed to rerank with a bias term that downgrades missing data.
4) Retrieval + reranker:
   - Index documents into your vector store (we support off-the-shelf connectors to Milvus/Elastic/Weaviate).
   - Hybrid rerank: candidate set from embedding cosine + BM25, then run a lightweight reranker model (125M-350M) in Redwood to produce final ordering.

Partial failure handling
- Timeouts: return best-effort candidates and surface a warning card to the user.
- Unknown tool: runtime will return a structured error; recommend a fallback tool "noop_handler" implemented to capture invalid tool calls for debugging.

Attachments included: redwood-sdk-quickstart.md (snippet for Node), and a small sample tool-def contract embedded.

Proposed next steps / owners
- Logan: share sandbox API keys and redwood SDK snippets (today) -> attached.
- Ben (Eng): technical sync to walk through routing & PCI plan (Mon 7/9 PST) -> Ben to take lead.
- Marissa (CS): POC acceptance criteria + test prompts (Mon 7/9 PST).

Would 30 minutes on Mon 7/9 at 10am PT work for a narrow technical sync? If yes, Ben will share an invite.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks Logan — that helps. Couple of clarifying Qs before the tech sync: 

1) Parallel tool pattern: If invoice_fetcher returns many candidates (e.g., 30 matches) and fraud_check returns a score per candidate, is it better to (A) merge all candidates then run a reranker over the whole set, or (B) prune by fraud score first, then rerank? Any production guidance on memory/latency tradeoffs?

2) Reranker model: Do you recommend running reranker in your hosted environment (lower ops) vs bringing a smaller reranker into our VPC? If we run in-hosted, what's the recommended tokenization/limit to avoid excessive costs?

3) Structured output enforcement: In edge cases where the model produces a tool name slightly different (typo), what's your recommended recovery path? Is there a mapping layer (alias table) we can configure?

4) Embedding index: we plan to use chunked embeddings for long invoices. Any guidance on chunk size and metadata (invoice_id, page_num) you recommend to make reranking efficient?

I'll also attach an anonymized sample invoice set (small) to the Drive link for benchmarking.

Appreciate the quick responses — we'll confirm the sync time after your availability.

Alex

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@bridgepoint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Jul 2028 09:43:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick recap + tech asks (tool calling + reranker)

Great questions — answers below with recommended defaults for a low-risk POC.

1) Merge vs prune (practical recommendation)
- Recommended default: prune with cheap heuristics first, then rerank the pruned set. Flow:
  a) invoice_fetcher returns candidates (cap at 100).
  b) Apply cheap filters: date/customer_id match, amount tolerance ±5%, and include fraud_check score if available.
  c) If candidate set > 25 after filters, randomly sample or apply a score threshold to reduce to ~25 for the reranker.
- Rationale: reranker models are more expensive per candidate; pruning reduces latency and cost while retaining high-quality candidates.

2) Reranker placement (hosted vs VPC)
- Hosted reranker is faster to iterate and we can autoscale; recommended for POC. For production where PCI-sensitive fields influence rerank, colocate reranker in VPC.
- Tokenization/limits: recommend batching candidates with max 25 snippets per request and a 2048-token cap for the reranker input. Use concise templates that include structured fields (invoice_id, snippet, candidate_score).

3) Tool name typos / aliases
- We support a configurable alias table for tool names at the routing layer. Runtime behavior: map aliases -> canonical tool id. If no mapping found, runtime returns an error with suggested close matches (Levenshtein) and invokes the noop_handler to preserve context.

4) Embedding chunking guidance
- Chunk size: 200-400 tokens per chunk works well for invoices (often 2-5 chunks per page).
- Metadata: include invoice_id, page_num, table_anchor flags, and a dense vector for signature blocks. Store original offset to allow assembly for context windows during rerank.

Sample tool-def (illustrative)
{
  "tool_name": "invoice_fetcher",
  "description": "Return candidate invoice records given a fuzzy query",
  "inputs": ["query_text", "customer_id", "date_range"],
  "outputs": ["invoice_id", "confidence", "snippet", "metadata"]
}

Fallback and error handling defaults
- Per-tool timeout default: 500ms (configurable).
- Retries: none for side-effectful tools (payment_processor). For idempotent reads (invoice_fetcher) we allow 1 retry with exponential backoff.
- Observability: every tool call emits a token-level trace and a correlation id; we recommend sending logs to your central aggregator with the correlation id so we can jointly troubleshoot.
